paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God was watching how Israel's neighbors treated them on their worst day. The Ammonites exclaimed, "Aha!" when Judah went into exile (Ezekiel 25:3). Edom acted vengefully, and the Philistines acted with "ancient hostility" (Ezekiel 25:12, 15). Cheering at somebody's bad day is NOT a small thing to God.

Notice the pattern, too. Ammon hears, "Then you will know that I am the LORD" (Ezekiel 25:5), and Moab and the Philistines are told they will know He is the LORD (Ezekiel 25:11, 17), while Edom hears, "Then they will know My vengeance" (Ezekiel 25:14). Nobody on that list got to say God wasn't paying attention. The God who cared about His people's pain is the same God who is the LORD over every nation, and that's good news for anybody who has ever been laughed at while they were down.

So what do we do with it, baker? We check our own hearts, because I have seen a smirk sneak up on people at the wrong moment. When somebody around us stumbles, God invites us to be the one who helps, not the one who claps and stomps. And if you're the one who got laughed at, take heart. God sees it, and He hasn't forgotten you.
